title: The Impact of Family-Based Human Capital on Corporate Innovation: Evidence from Sibling-Chairpersons in China
eligible_reason: Main identification is cross-sectional: chair_sibling (chairperson has siblings; changes within firm for only 72 of 1,481 family firms) with industry and year FE (no firm FE), 13 firm/chair controls, and a one-child-policy instrument (Table 3). The succession DiD (Table 7A) uses 56 family-succession firms (successions 2009-2015) with heirpost = Heir_Sibling x postyear plus Heir_Sibling and postyear main effects, industry + year FE (no firm FE) and controls; postyear is a post-succession indicator for all succession firms (an extra event-time regressor), and Table 7B adds relative-period dummies periodt* for all units. Table 4 Panel E adds firm FE but keeps controls and the two-way-switching chair_sibling.
design_notes: Replication_code.do on fambase.dta (6,768 rows). Table 2: reghdfe patentf1/citationf1 chair_sibling [$control], absorb(year ind), cluster stock (line 37). Table 3: IV/RD on one-child policy (OCP, cutoff). Tables 4-6: robustness, subsamples, interactions (xi: reg with i.year i.ind). Table 7A line 385: reghdfe patentf1 heirpost Heir_Sibling postyear $control, absorb(year ind). Table 7B: tpostmm* (Heir_Sibling x period) and periodt*. Later tables: board diversity, investment, returns, M&A CARs.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Succession sample: 56 firms with succession years 2009 (2), 2010 (5), 2011 (4), 2012 (6), 2013 (11), 2014 (12), 2015 (16); 22 heirs with siblings, 34 without; every firm experiences succession.

specs.exclusion_reason: no firm FE (industry FE only), extra post-succession regressor for all units, time-varying controls
specs.treatment_definition: heir with siblings after the succession year

data_files_note: Analysis data shipped (CSMAR-based, hand-collected sibling information).
